subject: Mythology
title: Icarus and the Hubris of Technology
description: A short lesson to help you apply Icarus and the Hubris of Technology.

hook.text: Icarus flew too close to the sun and his wax wings melted. Engineers still call catastrophic overreach 'Icarus moments.'

buildup.text: The Challenger disaster, Chernobyl, and the Titan submersible — each was called an Icarus story by the press.

discovery.text: The myth's real warning was not about flying. It was about ignoring expertise — Icarus's father told him the safe path.

twist.text: Silicon Valley loves Icarus rhetoric but reverses it — founders celebrate 'flying too close to the sun' as a virtue.

climax.text: A 3,000-year-old story about a boy and wax wings is now the default metaphor for technological hubris worldwide.

punchline.text: Every crashed prototype proves Daedalus right: ambition needs limits.

quiz.question: What is the deeper warning in the Icarus myth?
options: That humans should never attempt to fly
That ignoring expertise and safe limits leads to disaster
That the sun is dangerous and should be feared
